newsitem.title: USA: Chubb launches E&O coverage for insurers.
newsitem.headline: Chubb launches E&O coverage for insurers.

text.p: ATLANTA, April 15, Reuters - Chubb Corp said it has launched a new product to cover the errors and omissions of insurance companies.

"Insurance companies increasingly face legal actions as a result of professional misjudgments and oversights," Chubb assistant vice president Howard McClure said in introducing the new policy at the Risk and Insurance Management Society conference here.
"There are numerous lawsuits brought by policyholders for bad faith, failure to properly disclose risks and the sale of unsuitable products that have been well publicized in recent years," he said.
Chubb said the Insurance Company Professional Liability (ICPL) policy is available with limits up to $25 million on a primary or excess basis.
The policy offers worldwide coverage for a broad range of activities related to providing insurance and financial services to customers.
The policy is non-cancelable by Chubb except in cases of nonpayment of premium. The insured has the right to choose its own legal defense counsel, subject to the insurer's approval, Chubb said.

Chubb also announced at the conference that it has created a new coverage enhancement for directors and officers liability insurance policies to help companies manage the investigation costs associated with shareholder derivative demands.
Shareholders who suspect wrongdoing on the part of a director or officer of a company can demand that the company bring suit against the individual, Chubb said.
If the company does not consent to this derivative demand, shareholders may sue the director or officer, on behalf of the company, in a so-called derivative lawsuit.
Chubb said derivative actions represent about half the claims filed by shareholders based on a recent Watson Wyatt D&O survey.

Chubb said in the past, a company would have to absorb the investigation costs associated with the derivative demands, which could be substantial and were usually not covered by traditional directors and officers policies.
